what_happened: Research found that deploy-baseline-lib.sh (confirm+attribute pipeline built for the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint) is directly reusable for task 403's attribution open question, and that Move 4/5's conclusion-stage.md is a ready-made precedent for the new once-per-invocation shared-gate stage this task needs -- no new mechanism class had to be invented.

Planning needed no new library design: deploy-baseline-lib.sh already exports deploy_baseline_self_attributable_findings, a per-task (not whole-batch) attribution function, and orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh already builds a per-task modified_files map for the deploy-pending path. Both are directly reusable templates, which collapsed the attribution work from 'design a library' to 'call an existing function per task'.

Discovered during planning that Mechanism A would be inert prose without editing context/contracts/phase-closure.md: its no-promotion-without-evidence rule states a 'full' declaration is discharged ONLY by the complete gate set, which contractually overrides any dispatch-time narrowing directive. The research report did not name this file. Added it as a Phase 1 target plus a named risk row.

Phases 1-3 were implemented and verified before committing, then committed as three separate commits by file set rather than true per-objective green-substep commits. orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh carries edits from both Phase 2 (invocation_modified_files seeding) and Phase 3 (batch-gate-deferral build_args append plus cycle_plan_dispatch_hash comment); both landed in the Phase 2 commit since the file was staged as a whole. The plan file's phase-1/2/3 checklist annotations were also all applied in one batch script before the first commit, so the Phase 1 commit's plan-file hunk carries check-off annotations for phases 2 and 3 too. No functional impact: each phase's own verification (suites, diff read-throughs) was run and passed before any commit.

Live corroboration of this task's own problem statement: while running Phase 6's required complete verify-deploy.sh gate set, ps showed sibling tasks 404 and 406 concurrently running their own full run-all.sh/verify-deploy.sh batteries on the same host, with Gate 8's run-all.sh internally re-forking nested verify-deploy.sh instances for test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh -- the exact duplicated-suite-in-flight pattern this task's description cites as the motivating incident. This observation independently substantiates the design goal without needing a synthetic repro.

A prior background-launch attempt for the Phase 6 full gate run used 'setsid nohup bash verify-deploy.sh &' followed by a disown/pid-capture sequence that errored on disown (no job control in a non-interactive shell), but the backgrounded process had already started successfully each retry. Three retries left three duplicate full verify-deploy.sh process trees running concurrently (each internally forking its own Gate 8 run-all.sh battery) before the mistake was noticed via ps. Resolved by identifying each tree's ancestry precisely (ppid chain back to this session's own eval shells, confirmed via the unique scratchpad log/pid file paths in each command line) and sending SIGTERM to exactly those PIDs, leaving sibling tasks 404/406's own verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh trees untouched. No pkill -f was used, consistent with this task's own anti-pattern warning about broad process kills under gate contention.

Phase 5's wiring of the Move 4 batch gate stage into skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md grew that file from 22,335 B to 24,126 B, 1,626 B over its Gate 20 per-file ceiling (22,500 B) -- a genuine regression caused by this task's own Phase 5 commit (0b553f56f), not a sibling or pre-existing issue. Resolved in Phase 6 by replacing the inlined nohup/pid-capture/kill-0 bash code block with a one-paragraph pointer substituting variable/script names into Move 3's own already-documented identical idiom (removing a near-duplicate restatement), combining two new Context-References bullets into one, reclaiming 560 B to land at 23,566 B, then a reviewed dated ceiling move (following this config file's own established rounding convention) to 24,000 B, recorded in agent-system/extensions/core/context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json with a new dated derivation paragraph. That config file was added to task 403's state.json file_scope since it was not originally declared.

Gate 4 (check-task-references.sh) flags one unexempted task-reference occurrence at agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/task-reference-exemptions.md:48 -- an illustrative example citation ('Task 101: specs/101_remove_trivial_operator/summaries/01_summary.md') inside the exemption table's own row for the memory-vault path-level exemption, landed by commit acf5a523b ('core: make the memory vault a path-level task-reference exemption') at 17:46:05, which is outside this task's and siblings 404/406's declared file_scope and postdates this task's own Phase 1-5 commits. Pre-existing and unrelated to task 403; not fixed here to avoid stepping on unrelated concurrent work. Not previously enumerated in this dispatch's known-baseline list (Gate 20/Gate 3-lean/Gate 8), so recorded here for traceability.
